impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. ## Problem

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git calls in the same order.

Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-1010: CRAP decompression of four post-action modules

### What changed
Decomposed the five CRAP-hot functions (`action` in `postBugCreation`, `postBulkBugsCreation`, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput`; `createBatchEpic` in `createBugFixBatchEpic`; `extractKeyFromResult` in `postBulkBugsCreation`) into small single-purpose helpers following the existing `extractKeyFromResult`-style pattern, with no intentional behavior change.

### Key decisions
- Every extracted helper is a named module-level function with CC ≤ 8, so it stays under the `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8` ratchet for new functions at any coverage.
- Dispatch extracted via handler/lookup functions; `action` kept as thin orchestration (CC 2–5).
- Behavior pinned first with characterization tests (33 new tests, incl. first-ever suite for `createBugFixBatchEpic`), then refactored against them.
- Measured locally with the pinned `IstiN/crap4js` + `nyc` toolchain against the released `crap-baseline` asset.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3616 passed, 0 failed
```

<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[action] --> C[buildContext]
  C --> G{guards}
  G -->|early result| R[return]
  G -->|ok| D[dispatch / phase helpers]
  D --> H[small pure helpers: build*/try*/resolve*]
  H --> T[tracker wrappers]
```
</details>

## Description

## Problem
Ticket-creation post-steps: `createBugFixBatchEpic.js::createBatchEpic` **110**, `postBugCreation.js::action` **86.8**, `postBulkBugsCreation.js` `action` **82.8** and `extractKeyFromResult` **72**, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput.js::action` **86.8**. ## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git calls in the same order.

## Rules (read before starting)

Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? - Every extracted helper is a named module-level function with CC ≤ 8, so it stays under the `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8` ratchet for new functions at any coverage.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Decomposed the five CRAP-hot functions (`action` in `postBugCreation`, `postBulkBugsCreation`, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput`; `createBatchEpic` in `createBugFixBatchEpic`; `extractKeyFromResult` in `postBulkBugsCreation`) into small single-purpose helpers following the existing `extractKeyFromResult`-style pattern, with no intentional behavior change.

- Every extracted helper is a named module-level function with CC ≤ 8, so it stays under the `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8` ratchet for new functions at any coverage.

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. ## PR Description

Closes #1010
# gh-1010: CRAP decompression of four post-action modules

### What changed
Decomposed the five CRAP-hot functions (`action` in `postBugCreation`, `postBulkBugsCreation`, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput`; `createBatchEpic` in `createBugFixBatchEpic`; `extractKeyFromResult` in `postBulkBugsCreation`) into small single-purpose helpers following the existing `extractKeyFromResult`-style pattern, with no intentional behavior change.

### Key decisions
- Every extracted helper is a named module-level function with CC ≤ 8, so it stays under the `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8` ratchet for new functions at any coverage.
- Dispatch extracted via handler/lookup functions; `action` kept as thin orchestration (CC 2–5).
- Behavior pinned first with characterization tests (33 new tests, incl. first-ever suite for `createBugFixBatchEpic`), then refactored against them.
- Measured locally with the pinned `IstiN/crap4js` + `nyc` toolchain against the released `crap-baseline` asset.

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3616 passed, 0 failed
```
Quality-gate result vs the released baseline: `createBatchEpic` 110→2, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput.action` 86.8→5, `postBugCreation.action` 86.8→5, `postBulkBugsCreation.action` 82.8→3.1, `postBulkBugsCreation.extractKeyFromResult` 72→6; 0 regressions, 0 new-over-threshold, 11 improvements.

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[action] --> C[buildContext]
  C --> G{guards}
  G -->|early result| R[return]
  G -->|ok| D[dispatch / phase helpers]
  D --> H[small pure helpers: build*/try*/resolve*]
  H --> T[tracker wrappers]
```
</details>

# gh-1010: [CRAP] bug/story creation posts: createBugFixBatchEpic.createBatchEpic (110) + postBugCreation.action (87) + postBulkBugsCreation (action 83, extractKeyFromResult 72) + createPlannedStoriesFromOutput.action (87)

## Description

## Problem
Ticket-creation post-steps: `createBugFixBatchEpic.js::createBatchEpic` **110**, `postBugCreation.js::action` **86.8**, `postBulkBugsCreation.js` `action` **82.8** and `extractKeyFromResult` **72**, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput.js::action` **86.8**. Must stay correct for Jira, ADO and GitHub payload shapes.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR re…

- Every extracted helper is a named module-level function with CC ≤ 8, so it stays under the `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8` ratchet for new functions at any coverage.

- Measured locally with the pinned `IstiN/crap4js` + `nyc` toolchain against the released `crap-baseline` asset.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:

Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Decomposed the five CRAP-hot functions (`action` in `postBugCreation`, `postBulkBugsCreation`, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput`; `createBatchEpic` in `createBugFixBatchEpic`; `extractKeyFromResult` in `postBulkBugsCreation`) into small single-purpose helpers following the existing `extractKeyFromResult`-style pattern, with no intentional behavior change.

- Every extracted helper is a named module-level function with CC ≤ 8, so it stays under the `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8` ratchet for new functions at any coverage.

- Measured locally with the pinned `IstiN/crap4js` + `nyc` toolchain against the released `crap-baseline` asset.

flowchart TD

## Description

## Problem
Ticket-creation post-steps: `createBugFixBatchEpic.js::createBatchEpic` **110**, `postBugCreation.js::action` **86.8**, `postBulkBugsCreation.js` `action` **82.8** and `extractKeyFromResult` **72**, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput.js::action` **86.8**. ## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git calls in the same order.

- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).

Also old none path and link/create tail — fine.

re-read changed files,

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. ## Description

## Problem
Ticket-creation post-steps: `createBugFixBatchEpic.js::createBatchEpic` **110**, `postBugCreation.js::action` **86.8**, `postBulkBugsCreation.js` `action` **82.8** and `extractKeyFromResult` **72**, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput.js::action` **86.8**. ## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.

Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
