Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. ## Description

## Problem
Ticket-creation post-steps: `createBugFixBatchEpic.js::createBatchEpic` **110**, `postBugCreation.js::action` **86.8**, `postBulkBugsCreation.js` `action` **82.8** and `extractKeyFromResult` **72**, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput.js::action` **86.8**. ## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.

Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.

Differences:

# gh-1010: CRAP decompression of four post-action modules

### What changed
Decomposed the five CRAP-hot functions (`action` in `postBugCreation`, `postBulkBugsCreation`, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput`; `createBatchEpic` in `createBugFixBatchEpic`; `extractKeyFromResult` in `postBulkBugsCreation`) into small single-purpose helpers following the existing `extractKeyFromResult`-style pattern, with no intentional behavior change.

### Key decisions
- Every extracted helper is a named module-level function with CC ≤ 8, so it stays under the `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8` ratchet for new functions at any coverage.
- Dispatch extracted via handler/lookup functions; `action` kept as thin orchestration (CC 2–5).
- Behavior pinned first with characterization tests (33 new tests, incl. first-ever suite for `createBugFixBatchEpic`), then refactored against them.
- Measured locally with the pinned `IstiN/crap4js` + `nyc` toolchain against the released `crap-baseline` asset.

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json   # 3616 passed, 0 failed
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[action] --> C[buildContext]

  H --> T[tracker wrappers]
```
</details>

## Description

## Problem
Ticket-creation post-steps: `createBugFixBatchEpic.js::createBatchEpic` **110**, `postBugCreation.js::action` **86.8**, `postBulkBugsCreation.js` `action` **82.8** and `extractKeyFromResult` **72**, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput.js::action` **86.8**. ## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git calls in the same order.

- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). # gh-1010: CRAP decompression of four post-action modules

### What changed
Decomposed the five CRAP-hot functions (`action` in `postBugCreation`, `postBulkBugsCreation`, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput`; `createBatchEpic` in `createBugFixBatchEpic`; `extractKeyFromResult` in `postBulkBugsCreation`) into small single-purpose helpers following the existing `extractKeyFromResult`-style pattern, with no intentional behavior change.

### Key decisions
- Every extracted helper is a named module-level function with CC ≤ 8, so it stays under the `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8` ratchet for new functions at any coverage.
- Dispatch extracted via handler/lookup functions; `action` kept as thin orchestration (CC 2–5).
- Behavior pinned first with characterization tests (33 new tests, incl. first-ever suite for `createBugFixBatchEpic`), then refactored against them.
- Measured locally with the pinned `IstiN/crap4js` + `nyc` toolchain against the released `crap-baseline` asset.

# gh-1010: [CRAP] bug/story creation posts: createBugFixBatchEpic.createBatchEpic (110) + postBugCreation.action (87) + postBulkBugsCreation (action 83, extractKeyFromResult 72) + createPlannedStoriesFromOutput.action (87)

## Description

## Problem
Ticket-creation post-steps: `createBugFixBatchEpic.js::createBatchEpic` **110**, `postBugCreation.js::action` **86.8**, `postBulkBugsCreation.js` `action` **82.8** and `extractKeyFromResult` **72**, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput.js::action` **86.8**. Must stay correct for Jira, ADO and GitHub payload shapes.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. Decomposed the five CRAP-hot functions (`action` in `postBugCreation`, `postBulkBugsCreation`, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput`; `createBatchEpic` in `createBugFixBatchEpic`; `extractKeyFromResult` in `postBulkBugsCreation`) into small single-purpose helpers following the existing `extractKeyFromResult`-style pattern, with no intentional behavior change.

- Every extracted helper is a named module-level function with CC ≤ 8, so it stays under the `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8` ratchet for new functions at any coverage.

- Measured locally with the pinned `IstiN/crap4js` + `nyc` toolchain against the released `crap-baseline` asset.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[action] --> C[buildContext]

```

Old order:

4. skipLabelPresent && mode === 'reuse' → log reuse, continue

New order in `action`:
- `prepareStoryPlan` computes skipLabelPresent, skipLabelReuse, and **logs the reuse message immediately** (`logSkipLabelReuse`) — before the enabled/sourceTicketKey guards.
- `earlyPlanResult`: planGuardResult → enabled===false check first, then sourceTicketKey guard; then skipLabelGuardResult.

Differences:
- Old code checked enabled BEFORE computing skipLabelPresent; order of guard returns same relative precedence (enabled > missing key > skip label). New also: enabled → missing key → skip label. Same precedence.
- **Tracker creation timing**: old created tracker BEFORE the guards (`tracker = trackersModule.createTracker(null, customParams)` happened before enabled check). New also creates tracker in prepareStoryPlan before guards. Same.
- **Reuse-mode log line ordering**: Old logged reuse message after the strict-skip guard, i.e. only reached if enabled && sourceTicketKey present. New logs it in prepareStoryPlan — before the enabled/sourceTicketKey guards. So if `enabled === false` and label present+reuse, old: no log, returns disabled. New: logs "continuing in reuse mode" then returns disabled. Log line difference on an early-exit path — cosmetic, minor. Actually also if sourceTicketKey missing and reuse label present — new logs reuse line; old didn't. Minor.

2. **`customParams` resolution difference**:

New: `firstOf3(params.customParams, jobParams.customParams, {})` — same semantics.

# gh-1010: CRAP decompression of four post-action modules

### What changed
Decomposed the five CRAP-hot functions (`action` in `postBugCreation`, `postBulkBugsCreation`, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput`; `createBatchEpic` in `createBugFixBatchEpic`; `extractKeyFromResult` in `postBulkBugsCreation`) into small single-purpose helpers following the existing `extractKeyFromResult`-style pattern, with no intentional behavior change.

### Key decisions
- Every extracted helper is a named module-level function with CC ≤ 8, so it stays under the `CRAP_THRESHOLD=8` ratchet for new functions at any coverage.
- Dispatch extracted via handler/lookup functions; `action` kept as thin orchestration (CC 2–5).
- Behavior pinned first with characterization tests (33 new tests, incl. first-ever suite for `createBugFixBatchEpic`), then refactored against them.
- Measured locally with the pinned `IstiN/crap4js` + `nyc` toolchain against the released `crap-baseline` asset.

# gh-1010: [CRAP] bug/story creation posts: createBugFixBatchEpic.createBatchEpic (110) + postBugCreation.action (87) + postBulkBugsCreation (action 83, extractKeyFromResult 72) + createPlannedStoriesFromOutput.action (87)

## Description

## Problem
Ticket-creation post-steps: `createBugFixBatchEpic.js::createBatchEpic` **110**, `postBugCreation.js::action` **86.8**, `postBulkBugsCreation.js` `action` **82.8** and `extractKeyFromResult` **72**, `createPlannedStoriesFromOutput.js::action` **86.8**. Must stay correct for Jira, ADO and GitHub payload shapes.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

- `earlyPlanResult`: planGuardResult → enabled===false check first, then sourceTicketKey guard; then skipLabelGuardResult.

Differences:
- Old code checked enabled BEFORE computing skipLabelPresent; order of guard returns same relative precedence (enabled > missing key > skip label). New also: enabled → missing key → skip label. Same precedence.

## Problem

Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). createPlannedStoriesFromOutput comparison:

1. **Guard order difference (subtle behavior change)**: 

Old order:
1. config.enabled === false → skip
2. !sourceTicketKey → error
3. skipLabelPresent && mode !== 'reuse' → skip
4. skipLabelPresent && mode === 'reuse' → log reuse, continue

New order in `action`:
- `prepareStoryPlan` computes skipLabelPresent, skipLabelReuse, and **logs the reuse message immediately** (`logSkipLabelReuse`) — before the enabled/sourceTicketKey guards.
- `earlyPlanResult`: planGuardResult → enabled===false check first, then sourceTicketKey guard; then skipLabelGuardResult.

Differences:
- Old code checked enabled BEFORE computing skipLabelPresent; order of guard returns same relative precedence (enabled > missing key > skip label). New also: enabled → missing key → skip label. Same precedence.
- **Tracker creation timing**: old created tracker BEFORE the guards (`tracker = trackersModule.createTracker(null, customParams)` happened before enabled check). New also creates tracker in prepareStoryPlan before guards. Same.
- **Reuse-mode log line ordering**: Old logged reuse message after the strict-skip guard, i.e. only reached if enabled && sourceTicketKey present. New logs it in prepareStoryPlan — before the enabled/sourceTicketKey guards. So if `enabled === false` and label present+reuse, old: no log, returns disabled. New: logs "continuing in reuse mode" then returns disabled. Log line difference on an early-exit path — cosmetic, minor. Actually also if sourceTicketKey missing and reuse label present — new logs reuse line; old didn't. Minor.

2. **`customParams` resolution difference**:

Old: `var customParams = (params.customParams) || (jobParams.customParams) || {};`
New: `firstOf3(params.customParams, jobParams.customParams, {})` — same semantics.

`jobParams`: old `params.jobParams || {}`. New: `firstObject(params.jobParams, {})`. same.

3. `outputFile`: same. `readStoriesJson`, guards same.

4. Story loop: old `var entry = stories[i] || {}`; new `firstObject(stories[i], {})`. same.

5. `resolvedParentKey`: same.

createPlannedStoriesFromOutput comparison:

1. **Guard order difference (subtle behavior change)**: 

Old order:
1. config.enabled === false → skip
2. !sourceTicketKey → error
3. skipLabelPresent && mode !== 'reuse' → skip
4. skipLabelPresent && mode === 'reuse' → log reuse, continue

New order in `action`:
- `prepareStoryPlan` computes skipLabelPresent, skipLabelReuse, and **logs the reuse message immediately** (`logSkipLabelReuse`) — before the enabled/sourceTicketKey guards.
- `earlyPlanResult`: planGuardResult → enabled===false check first, then sourceTicketKey guard; then skipLabelGuardResult.

Differences:
- Old code checked enabled BEFORE computing skipLabelPresent; order of guard returns same relative precedence (enabled > missing key > skip label). New also: enabled → missing key → skip label. Same precedence.
- **Tracker creation timing**: old created tracker BEFORE the guards (`tracker = trackersModule.createTracker(null, customParams)` happened before enabled check). New also creates tracker in prepareStoryPlan before guards. Same.
- **Reuse-mode log line ordering**: Old logged reuse message after the strict-skip guard, i.e. only reached if enabled && sourceTicketKey present. New logs it in prepareStoryPlan — before the enabled/sourceTicketKey guards. So if `enabled === false` and label present+reuse, old: no log, returns disabled. New: logs "continuing in reuse mode" then returns disabled. Log line difference on an early-exit path — cosmetic, minor. Actually also if sourceTicketKey missing and reuse label present — new logs reuse line; old didn't. Minor.

2. **`customParams` resolution difference**:

Old: `var customParams = (params.customParams) || (jobParams.customParams) || {};`
New: `firstOf3(params.customParams, jobParams.customParams, {})` — same semantics.

`jobParams`: old `params.jobParams || {}`. New: `firstObject(params.jobParams, {})`. same.

3. `outputFile`: same. `readStoriesJson`, guards same.

4. Story loop: old `var entry = stories[i] || {}`; new `firstObject(stories[i], {})`. same.

5. `resolvedParentKey`: same.

6. `existingByParent` lazy fetch: same via parentStoryMap.

7. `existingKey = existingByParent[resolvedParentKey][summary] || null` vs new `firstObject(parentMap[summary], null)`. If summaryToKey has summary mapped to a falsy value... only set when issue.key truthy? `summaryToKey[summary] = issue.key` — issue.key could be undefined in theory; then old: `map[summary] || null` = null; new firstObject(undefined, null) = null. same.

8. blockedBy loop: old `var blockedByRelationship = config.blockedByRelationship || 'Blocks'` computed per story; new per-link via tryBlockerLink (`firstObject(plan.config.blockedByRelationship, 'Blocks')`). Same value.

Old: catch link error → warn, anyBlocked unchanged (stays previous value). New attemptBlockerLink returns anyBlocked on error. Same.

Move to blocked: old `if (anyBlocked && config.blockedStatusName !== false)`. New: moveBlockedStory → moveToBlockedStatus → if blockedStatusName === false return; tryMoveToBlocked. Same.

9. integrates: same. Old `if (!otherKey || otherKey === storyKey) continue;` new tryIntegratesLink returns. Same.

10. Summary comment & label: same.

11. Return message: same.

One more: in old code, `keyMap[createdKey] = createdKey` etc. New recordCreatedKey does the same plus parentMap[summary] = createdKey. Same.

`processStoryEntry`: `var summary = buildSummary(entry.summary, i)`. Old same. Note createStory uses `buildSummary(entry.summary, 0)` internally — same in both.

So createPlannedStoriesFromOutput is faithful except the cosmetic log ordering in reuse mode.

Now postBugCreation: I checked. One difference I noted: `removeSmTriggerLabel` logs '✅ Removed SM trigger label:' — old code in tests_pass/none branches did NOT log that. Minor. Also in the old link/create tail, removal of 'sm_test_automation_triggered' was logged ('✅ Removed sm_test_automation_triggered'); new `removeLabelQuietly` doesn't log. Minor log difs.

Another check in postBugCreation: `buildActionContext` — old created tracker with `(params.jobParams && params.jobParams.customParams) || params.customParams || {}`. New: same expression. OK.

`handleTestsPassDecision` in new returns `{success: true, ticketKey, bugKey: null, action: 'tests_pass'}` — matches old.

But wait — old `tests_pass` and `none` branches removed smTriggerLabel WITHOUT logging; new removeSmTriggerLabel logs on success. Also old none-branch: `if (smTriggerLabel) { try { tracker.removeLabel } catch {} }` — no console.log. New logs. So there are extra log lines in none/tests_pass paths. Very minor; the ticket said "same log lines" — worth a SUGESTION at most. Also dropped log line in the link/create tail (Removed sm_test_automation_triggered). Minor.

Also old code: link/create tail always attempted removeLabel('sm_test_automation_triggered') with a console.log inside try — if removeLabel threw, the log never printed. New removeLabelQuietly: never logs. So a log line "✅ Removed sm_test_automation_triggered" disappeared from output. Also `moveFailedTcToRework` still logs it. These are log-parity nitpicks — SUGESTION level at most. I probably won't flag these individually; maybe one SUGESTION summarizing log parity.

## Description

## Problem

## Goal

Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. Comparing postBugCreation old vs new for behavior differences:

Old flow for `create` branch:
- build description, check !summary → report missing.
- try createTicket → bugKey = extractKeyFromResult(result)
- if bugKey: linkBugToTC directly (throws propagate! Actually linkBugToTC is called NOT inside try in the `if (bugKey)` block... wait, look: it's inside the outer `try { var result = tracker.createTicket...` block. `linkBugToTC(tracker, ticketKey, bugKey);` — if it throws, it goes to `catch (e) { console.error('Failed to create bug:', e); comment = 'h3. ❌ Bug Creation Failed...' }`. So in the OLD code, if linking after create threw, the comment was "Bug Creation Failed" and bugLinked stays false, bugKey remains set (it was assigned before the throw!). Actually `bugKey = extractKeyFromResult(result)` was assigned before the link attempt, so bugKey stays set even though link failed. And comment = CreateFailed. bugLinked = false.

New code: tryCreateBug catches create errors → ok:false. Then outcomeForCreatedKey: tryLinkBugToTc catches link errors separately → comment = buildCreateFailedComment(link.error), bugLinked: link.ok, bugKey kept. Same outcome: comment is CreateFailed with the link error message (old showed link error too since `e` is the link error). Same.

Old: create throws → catch → comment = CreateFailed(e), bugKey stays null (assignment never happened). New: attempt.ok=false → buildCreateOutcome → CreateFailed(attempt.error), bugKey null. Same.

Old tests_pass: postComment try, moveToStatusOrMark try, removeLabel wipLabel try, remove smTriggerLabel try, return. New handleTestsPassDecision: tryPostComment, moveTcToPassed, removeLabelQuietly wip, removeSmTriggerLabel. Same. Note old logs nothing about removing sm trigger label in tests_pass path (no console.log). removeSmTriggerLabel logs '✅ Removed SM trigger label:' on success — old code in tests_pass path did NOT log that (just `try { tracker.removeLabel(...) } catch {}` with no log). Minor log line addition: new removeSmTriggerLabel logs on success; old only logged in the link/create tail. Ticket rule says "same log lines/side effects". This is a minor difference — new log line appears in tests_pass and none paths. Actually wait, in old none path: `if (smTriggerLabel) { try { tracker.removeLabel(ticketKey, smTriggerLabel); } catch (e) {} }` — no log. New: removeSmTriggerLabel logs '✅ Removed SM trigger label:' when successful. So one extra console.log line in tests_pass/none paths. Very minor; arguably fine but a deviation from "same log lines".

Also old none path and link/create tail — fine.

Another subtle difference: in old code for the `none` action, when smTriggerLabel exists and removeLabel succeeds, no log; new logs. Also in the old link/create path, `console.log('✅ Removed SM trigger label:', smTriggerLabel)` appears; new removeSmTriggerLabel preserves that.

Also `removeLabelQuietly(tracker, ticketKey, 'sm_test_automation_triggered')` — old logged '✅ Removed sm_test_automation_triggered' on success in the tail; new removeLabelQuietly does not log. So a log line was dropped in the link/create tail (the old code had `console.log('✅ Removed sm_test_automation_triggered')` inside the try after removeLabel in the main tail; note moveFailedTcToRework also removes that label with log, but in the link/create tail the old code logged). Minor log differences — not worth blocking.

Behavior check on reportMissingDecision: old posted comment NOT in try — if postComment throws, it propagates to outer catch → reportActionFailure. New: reportMissingDecision also posts without try. Same.

One more: old code `var customParams = params.jobParams && params.jobParams.customParams;` computed AFTER createTracker but used... same.

Error path: old catch uses `tracker` which may be undefined if createTracker threw → `tracker.postComment` would throw inside try → caught by inner try. New: reportActionFailure checks `ctx ? ctx.tracker : null` and if tracker null, skips posting. Slightly safer. Same behavior when tracker exists.

dispatchDecision: old used if/else if chain: link requires existingKey; if action=='link' without existingKey → falls to else (none handler). New: `decision.action === 'link' && decision.existingKey` false → not create, not tests_pass → handleNoneDecision. Same.

createPlannedStoriesFromOutput comparison:

1. **Guard order difference (subtle behavior change)**: 

Old order:
1. config.enabled === false → skip
2. !sourceTicketKey → error
3. skipLabelPresent && mode !== 'reuse' → skip
4. skipLabelPresent && mode === 'reuse' → log reuse, continue

New order in `action`:
- `prepareStoryPlan` computes skipLabelPresent, skipLabelReuse, and **logs the reuse message immediately** (`logSkipLabelReuse`) — before the enabled/sourceTicketKey guards.
- `earlyPlanResult`: planGuardResult → enabled===false check first, then sourceTicketKey guard; then skipLabelGuardResult.

Differences:
- Old code checked enabled BEFORE computing skipLabelPresent; order of guard returns same relative precedence (enabled > missing key > skip label). New also: enabled → missing key → skip label. Same precedence.
- **Tracker creation timing**: old created tracker BEFORE the guards (`tracker = trackersModule.createTracker(null, customParams)` happened before enabled check). New also creates tracker in prepareStoryPlan before guards. Same.
- **Reuse-mode log line ordering**: Old logged reuse message after the strict-skip guard, i.e. only reached if enabled && sourceTicketKey present. New logs it in prepareStoryPlan — before the enabled/sourceTicketKey guards. So if `enabled === false` and label present+reuse, old: no log, returns disabled. New: logs "continuing in reuse mode" then returns disabled. Log line difference on an early-exit path — cosmetic, minor. Actually also if sourceTicketKey missing and reuse label present — new logs reuse line; old didn't. Minor.

2. **`customParams` resolution difference**:

Old: `var customParams = (params.customParams) || (jobParams.customParams) || {};`
New: `firstOf3(params.customParams, jobParams.customParams, {})` — same semantics.

`jobParams`: old `params.jobParams || {}`. New: `firstObject(params.jobParams, {})`. same.

3. `outputFile`: same. `readStoriesJson`, guards same.

4. Story loop: old `var entry = stories[i] || {}`; new `firstObject(stories[i], {})`. same.

5. `resolvedParentKey`: same.

6. `existingByParent` lazy fetch: same via parentStoryMap.

7. `existingKey = existingByParent[resolvedParentKey][summary] || null` vs new `firstObject(parentMap[summary], null)`. If summaryToKey has summary mapped to a falsy value... only set when issue.key truthy? `summaryToKey[summary] = issue.key` — issue.key could be undefined in theory; then old: `map[summary] || null` = null; new firstObject(undefined, null) = null. same.

8. blockedBy loop: old `var blockedByRelationship = config.blockedByRelationship || 'Blocks'` computed per story; new per-link via tryBlockerLink (`firstObject(plan.config.blockedByRelationship, 'Blocks')`). Same value.

Old: catch link error → warn, anyBlocked unchanged (stays previous value). New attemptBlockerLink returns anyBlocked on error. Same.

Move to blocked: old `if (anyBlocked && config.blockedStatusName !== false)`. New: moveBlockedStory → moveToBlockedStatus → if blockedStatusName === false return; tryMoveToBlocked. Same.

9. integrates: same. Old `if (!otherKey || otherKey === storyKey) continue;` new tryIntegratesLink returns. Same.

10. Summary comment & label: same.

11. Return message: same.

One more: in old code, `keyMap[createdKey] = createdKey` etc. New recordCreatedKey does the same plus parentMap[summary] = createdKey. Same.

`processStoryEntry`: `var summary = buildSummary(entry.summary, i)`. Old same. Note createStory uses `buildSummary(entry.summary, 0)` internally — same in both.

So createPlannedStoriesFromOutput is faithful except the cosmetic log ordering in reuse mode.

Now postBugCreation: I checked. One difference I noted: `removeSmTriggerLabel` logs '✅ Removed SM trigger label:' — old code in tests_pass/none branches did NOT log that. Minor. Also in the old link/create tail, removal of 'sm_test_automation_triggered' was logged ('✅ Removed sm_test_automation_triggered'); new `removeLabelQuietly` doesn't log. Minor log difs.

Another check in postBugCreation: `buildActionContext` — old created tracker with `(params.jobParams && params.jobParams.customParams) || params.customParams || {}`. New: same expression. OK.

`handleTestsPassDecision` in new returns `{success: true, ticketKey, bugKey: null, action: 'tests_pass'}` — matches old.

But wait — old `tests_pass` and `none` branches removed smTriggerLabel WITHOUT logging; new removeSmTriggerLabel logs on success. Also old none-branch: `if (smTriggerLabel) { try { tracker.removeLabel } catch {} }` — no console.log. New logs. So there are extra log lines in none/tests_pass paths. Very minor; the ticket said "same log lines" — worth a SUGESTION at most. Also dropped log line in the link/create tail (Removed sm_test_automation_triggered). Minor.

Also old code: link/create tail always attempted removeLabel('sm_test_automation_triggered') with a console.log inside try — if removeLabel threw, the log never printed. arguments.content:
💡 **SUGGESTION: Missing-decisions guard narrowed from falsy-check to `=== null`**

The old code treated any falsy parsed value as "missing" (`if (!decisions)`), which routes degenerate payloads (`""`, `0`, `false`) into the feedback-loop recovery. The new check `ctx.decisions === null` only catches an absent/unparseable file — a decisions file containing valid JSON `false` or `""` now silently runs an empty batch (`{success: true, results: {created: [], …}}`) instead of resuming the agent.

Low real-world risk (the AI writes an object), but `!ctx.decisions` preserves the original behavior exactly at zero cost.

💡 **SUGGESTION: Log-line parity vs the original flow**

Two tiny deviations from the ticket's "same log lines/side effects" rule, both caused by consolidating label removal:

1. `removeSmTriggerLabel` logs `✅ Removed SM trigger label:` on success — in the original code the `tests_pass` and `none` branches removed the SM label **silently** (only the link/create tail logged). Two new log lines now appear on those paths.
2. Conversely, the original link/create tail logged `✅ Removed sm_test_automation_triggered` after removing it; `removeLabelQuietly` drops that line.

Harmless, but if downstream log-scraping ever relies on these markers (the repo does grep logs in several recovery agents), restore the exact lines.

💡 **SUGGESTION: Reuse-mode log now emitted before the early-exit guards**

`logSkipLabelReuse(plan)` runs inside `prepareStoryPlan`, i.e. before the `enabled === false` and missing-source-ticket-key guards. In the original, the "continuing in reuse mode" line only printed when the action actually proceeded past those guards. Now a disabled or misconfigured run with the skip label present prints the reuse line and then immediately returns `skipped`/`error` — a slightly misleading log sequence. Moving the call after `earlyPlanResult` (or into the guard chain) restores the original ordering.

💡 **SUGGESTION: Runtime state file committed to the PR**

`.fah/bash_jobs/running.json` is live agent-session state (the list of in-flight background jobs), not source. This hunk just clears a stale snapshot, but:

- it is unrelated churn in a behavior-preserving refactor PR (scope creep),
- the file is rewritten by the runtime on every agent session, so touching it invites merge conflicts with any concurrent run.

Please revert this file (`git checkout origin/main -- .fah/bash_jobs/running.json`) to keep the diff limited to the refactor. Content-wise nothing sensitive leaked (env values were masked), so no security action needed.
